name: registry_rescore_weekly
description: Weekly surgical rescore (chairman directive 2026-07-14). Single resumable entrypoint tools/rescore/weekly_rescore.py replaces the manual fire_score.py path. Delta mode: never-scored distinct-URL servers + oldest-scored refresh cohort (cap 20k), newest_scored_at advances weekly, ~$0.3-0.6/run. Driven end-to-end by ONE scheduled task via --run; see scheduled_by and refresh_cycle_weeks below for the two figures this line stated wrongly.
no_loss_invariants: I1 scored_servers after import >= before (breach aborts loudly)
I2 preds coverage < 90% of export => run reports DEGRADED (partial results still ingested, never discarded)
I3 forensics (onstart.log) pulled from results/-fail branch BEFORE destroy
I4 instance always destroyed by end of collect (deadline + $ ceiling breach => forensics + destroy + ALERT)
I5 adapter sha256 pin verified before every launch
ledger: D:/zo/runs/weekly_rescore/ledger.jsonl (vast-jobs-daily-audit live-instance check is the backstop)
post_steps_automated: apply_risk_tier_backfill --apply (direct stamp ONLY; URL propagation deleted 2026-07-14, CofC FATHER R1)
scheduled_by: moat-rescore-weekly, cron `0 2 * * 2`, ONE task, drives `--run` end-to-end. CORRECTED 2026-08-04: this file previously claimed a two-task split (`weekly-rescore-fire` Tue + `weekly-rescore-collect` Tue+4h). NO SUCH TASKS EXIST -- resolved from the RUNTIME scheduler (list_scheduled_tasks), not from prose. `--phase fire-all|collect-all` still work, but nothing schedules them, so anyone who trusted this field and fired `fire-all` alone would leave a PAID instance running with no collector until the I4 deadline reaped it.
refresh_cycle_weeks: ~14. BASIS: 280,811 scored servers / 20,000 refresh_cap per week, measured 2026-08-04 from https://mcprisky.io/freshness. CORRECTED: the `<= ~4 weeks` claim removed from `description` was calibrated when the moat held ~80k servers and outlived its unit. Corroborated independently by `oldest_scored_at` = 2026-06-24, 5.9 weeks old at time of writing and growing. This does NOT affect `newest_scored_at`, the 7-day SLA metric, which advances on every wave; what stretches is per-SERVER score age.
